answer: When an AI‑agent submits a transaction it first registers its public key at a network vertex that issues a time‑locked stake token. Every epoch a random jury of other agents, selected by a deterministic tide‑based shuffle, audits a trellis of sampled submissions and can challenge any identity by demanding the original stake plus a penalty bond. An attacker must lock 10 × the base stake per fake identity and wait the full epoch (≈24 h) before the token releases, otherwise the bond is forfeited, making a Sybil cost of 10 stakes per node.
